launchColor.name: Silbermetallic (Annahme)
launchColor.note: 356 A introduced autumn 1955 (IAA Frankfurt). No source found naming the colour of the first show or press car; silver is a best guess.

porsche-356-356-a-coupe.note: Production 21,045 is the whole 356 A series (Coupé, Cabriolet, Speedster). 60 PS / 1582 cc refers to the 1600 version. 356 A list prices ranged from 11,400 to 15,750 DM depending on version; no single Coupé 1600 price verified.

launchColor.name: Rot (vermutlich Signalrot)
launchColor.note: US importer Max Hoffman first showed the red prototype #80002 at the Watkins Glen races, 17-18 Sept 1954; the name "Speedster" appeared in a Porsche press release the following week. Exact paint name not documented; early cars were offered in Speedster Blue, red and white.

porsche-356-356-speedster.note: Production 4,854 (all years) per en.wikipedia. Price: 12,200 DM ex works at introduction (de.wikipedia, year not stated; US price 1954 was US$2,995). Engines varied (1500: 55 PS, 1500 S: 70 PS, 1600: 60/75 PS), so no single power figure given.

porsche-356-356-carrera-2.note: 436 = 310 on 356 B (T6) + 126 on 356 C, per several secondary sources (not Wikipedia). Price 23,700 DM for the Coupé per de.wikipedia (year not stated; assumed 1962).

porsche-912-912-coupe.note: 30,745 is total 912 production 1965-69 incl. ~2,500 Targa (en.wikipedia: nearly 30,000 Coupés).

launchColor.name: Vipergrün Diamant (Viper Green Diamond)
launchColor.note: Series-production 911 Turbo 3.0 unveiled 3 Oct 1974 at the Paris Motor Show, "Painted in Viper Green Diamond" with black leather and tartan seat centres (Porsche Newsroom). Hex is an approximation of the metallic green. (The 1973 IAA Turbo study was silver.)

porsche-930-turbo-3-0.note: Production: 2,850 per Porsche (first three years); de.wikipedia gives 2,876, en.wikipedia 2,819.

launchColor.name: Indischrot (Guards Red)
launchColor.note: Introduced for model year 1978. No source found naming the colour of the first show or press car; Guards Red is a best guess.

porsche-930-turbo-3-3.note: Production 17,381 per de.wikipedia (en.wikipedia: 18,770). Price is the 1989 coupé list price; no 1978 launch price found.

launchColor.name: Grand-Prix-Weiß (Grand Prix White)
launchColor.note: Special-order (Sonderwunsch) option from 1981, series option M505/M506 from 1986/87; no public launch car documented. Porsche's own slantnose story is illustrated with a white car; the first Sonderwunsch road car (for Mansour Ojjeh) was Brilliant Red, the early factory prototype WP0ZZZ93ZBS000136 Montego Black metallic.

porsche-930-turbo-3-3-flachbau.note: 948 = 58 handbuilt with bumper headlights + 204 handbuilt with pop-up lights + 686 series cars (Porsche Exclusive, from 1984/86). 330 PS applies with the factory WLS power kit (from 1983/84). Conversion cost up to 27,500 DM (1985) on top of the Turbo price.
